description: REAL ActiveSupport::MessageVerifier output signed with the Turbo verifier key but wrapped in the `_rails` metadata envelope (purpose and/or expiry). Turbo::StreamsChannel never produces these, and the relay's Turbo profile implements no metadata, so it must reject them: expect.stream is null and expect.rejected is true (expect.turbo_rails_verified records what Rails' own verifier would say). The signature IS valid — the rejection is about the payload shape, not the HMAC.

producer.key_source: Rails.application.key_generator.generate_key("turbo/signed_stream_verifier_key") in a real application; pinned raw bytes here

rust_contract.key: base64-decode input.key_base64 to raw bytes; key it into SecretBytes/MessageVerifier
rust_contract.reject: MessageVerifier::new(key).verify(input.signed_stream_name) must be Err (the payload is not a JSON string); StreamsController.resolve(input.identifier) must not yield a stream
rust_contract.signature: HMAC-SHA256(key, expect.encoded_payload) == expect.signature still holds: a verifier that rejects on signature here is rejecting for the wrong reason
rust_contract.mismatch_rule: a case with "rust_status": "mismatch" documents real turbo-rails output the current verifier does NOT accept; assert the documented rejection, do not silently loosen the verifier

cases.name: purpose_metadata_envelope
cases.description: MessageVerifier#generate("demo", purpose: :orbitcast_fixture): the payload is a {"_rails":{...}} object, not a JSON string. Correctly signed with the Turbo key, and still not a stream name.

cases.name: expiry_metadata_envelope
cases.description: MessageVerifier#generate("demo", expires_at: 2100-01-01T00:00:00Z): an unexpired envelope with no purpose. turbo-rails' verifier unwraps it to "demo" (turbo_rails_verified), but Turbo::StreamsChannel never emits it and the relay implements no metadata: still an object, still rejected — the Turbo profile carries no expiry claim and must not grow one by accident.
